sections.title: Section 1 · Notice Inviting Bid (NIB)
sections.hint: Summary block: issuer name, work title, budget, EMD/tender fee, timeline, contact, portal link.
sections.body:
The Department of Public Works hereby invites bids for the Renovation of the City Park. The estimated budget for this project is $250,000. Interested bidders must submit a bid along with an Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) of $5,000 and a non-refundable tender fee of $300.

The timeline for bid submission is as follows:

  • Bid Opening Date: January 15, 2024
  • Bid Submission Deadline: December 30, 2023

For queries, contact the Procurement Office at procurement@publicworks.gov or call (123) 456-7890. Additional details and documentation can be accessed via our online portal: http://www.publicworks.gov/tenders.

sections.title: Section 2 · Instructions to Bidders (ITB)
sections.hint: How to submit, envelope structure, DSC class, portal URL, amendments, forfeiture, evaluation method.
sections.body:
Instructions to Bidders (ITB)

All bids must be submitted electronically through the designated procurement portal at www.example-portal.com. Bidders are required to structure their submission envelopes as follows:

  • Technical Proposal
  • Financial Proposal
  • Supporting Documents

Ensure you utilize a Class II Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) for signing the documents. Any amendments to this tender will be communicated through the portal, and it is the bidder's responsibility to stay updated.

Failure to comply with submission guidelines may result in bid forfeiture. The evaluation method will follow a two-stage process, assessing both technical and financial criteria.

sections.title: Section 3 · Qualifying Criteria
sections.hint: Turnover floor, similar-work rules, net-worth / bank cert, disqualifications, technical/financial weightage.
sections.body:
Qualifying Criteria

To be eligible for consideration, bidders must meet the following qualifying criteria:

  • Turnover: A minimum annual turnover of $500,000 in the last three financial years is required.
  • Similar Work Experience: Bidders must have completed at least three projects of similar scope and size within the past five years.
  • Net Worth: A minimum net worth of $300,000, supported by a bank certificate, is mandatory.
  • Disqualifications: Any bidder with a record of significant legal disputes in the past three years may be disqualified.
  • Evaluation Weightage: Technical proposals will account for 60%, while financial proposals will contribute 40% to the overall assessment.

header.eligibility: Central / State Govt Organizations / PSU / Autonomous Body per GFR 2017 Rule 133(3)

sections.title: Section 1 · Notice Inviting Bid (NIB)
sections.hint: Summary block: issuer name, work title, budget, EMD/tender fee, timeline, contact, portal link.
sections.body:
The Department of Public Works invites bids for the project titled Infrastructure Development Works. The total budget allocated for this project is 50,000,000 INR.

Participants are required to submit a Bid Security (EMD) of 1,000,000 INR and pay a non-refundable tender fee of 5,000 INR to be eligible for consideration.

This tender is open to Central / State Government Organizations, Public Sector Undertakings, and Autonomous Bodies as per the GFR 2017 Rule 133(3).

The evaluation of the bids will be conducted using the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, with a weightage of 70% for Technical Evaluation and 30% for Financial Evaluation.

Interested parties can access the tender documents and additional information through the Public Procurement Portal.

The timeline for the submission of bids is set for a period of 900 days from the date of this notice. For any inquiries, please contact our office at the details provided on the portal.

We look forward to your participation in this significant project aimed at improving our infrastructure capabilities.

sections.title: Section 2 · Instructions to Bidders (ITB)
sections.hint: How to submit, envelope structure, DSC class, portal URL, amendments, forfeiture, evaluation method.
sections.body:
All bidders are advised to follow these instructions meticulously to ensure a smooth submission process. The tender submission must be completed and submitted via the designated online portal.


Envelope Structure:

  • Envelope 1: Pre-qualification and Technical Proposal
  • Envelope 2: Financial Proposal

The bids must be submitted electronically with the required Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) to authenticate the submissions. Ensure that all mandatory documents are uploaded correctly to avoid rejection.


Portal URL: For submitting bids, please visit the following link: [Insert Portal URL]. All submissions should be made through this platform within the specified time frame.


Amendments: Any amendments to the tender will be published on the portal. It is the responsibility of the bidders to stay updated on any changes and to adjust their proposals accordingly.


Forfeiture: Please note that if the successful bidder fails to comply with the terms specified in the tender document or does not deliver as expected, the earnest money deposit may be forfeited.


Evaluation Method: The bids will be evaluated using the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method. The technical proposal will weigh 70% and the financial proposal will weigh 30% in the final evaluation.

sections.title: Section 3 · Qualifying Criteria
sections.hint: Turnover floor, similar-work rules, net-worth / bank cert, disqualifications, technical/financial weightage.
sections.body:
The qualifying criteria for this tender are established to ensure that the applicants possess the necessary expertise and financial capability to deliver the required services effectively. All applicants must meet the following minimum criteria:


  • Annual Turnover: Applicants must demonstrate a minimum annual turnover as specified in the tender documents. This threshold will help ensure that only financially stable entities can participate.
  • Experience in Similar Work: Applicants must have successfully completed similar projects in the past. Specific details regarding the number of projects and the nature of work will be outlined in the tender documentation.
  • Net Worth/Bank Certification: A certificate from a bank or a financial institution confirming the applicant's net worth should be provided.
  • Disqualifications: The following conditions may lead to disqualification:
    • Involvement in any unethical practices or fraudulent activities.
    • History of failed projects that have not been resolved amicably.
    • Non-compliance with previous contract obligations.
  • Evaluation Method: The evaluation of bids will be conducted using the QCBS (Quality and Cost Based Selection) method, with a weightage of 70% for technical criteria and 30% for financial proposals.

All submissions must comply with the conditions set above for eligibility, which includes entities registered as Central or State Government Organizations, PSUs, or Autonomous Bodies adhering to GFR 2017 Rule 133(3).

sections.title: Section 4 · Financial Bid Format
sections.hint: How the bidder quotes (percentage/lumpsum), decimals rule, taxes, currency.
sections.body:
This section outlines the format for submitting the financial bid as part of the tender application. Bidders must ensure that their proposals adhere strictly to the guidelines provided below to ensure compliance and facilitate smooth evaluation.

Bidders are required to submit their financial bids in the following format:

  • Bid Type: Bidders may choose to provide their quotes as either a percentage of the estimated cost or as a lumpsum amount. The chosen method must be clearly indicated in the bid submission.
  • Decimals Rule: All quoted values should be rounded to two decimal places. Bids quoted with more than two decimal places may be considered non-compliant.
  • Taxes: The financial proposal must distinctly include all applicable taxes. It is essential that bidders specify the tax rates applied and ensure that they are in accordance with regulatory requirements.
  • Currency: All monetary values must be quoted in Indian Rupees (INR). Any bids submitted in different currencies will be deemed invalid.

As outlined in the evaluation method, financial bids will constitute 30% of the overall scoring, with technical proposals accounting for 70%. Therefore, it is imperative that all financial submissions are both accurate and competitive to ensure consideration during the evaluation process.

sections.title: Annexure I · Acceptance of Bid Conditions
sections.hint: Bidder's undertaking that all terms and conditions of the tender are accepted without deviation.
sections.body:
This annexure serves as an essential component of the bidding process, establishing the Bidder's unequivocal commitment to adhere to all terms and conditions set forth in the tender document. By signing this section, the Bidder acknowledges full understanding and acceptance of the stipulated guidelines without any deviations.


By accepting this Annexure, the Bidder confirms that they meet the eligibility criteria as specified, which includes being a Central or State Government Organization, a Public Sector Undertaking (PSU), or an Autonomous Body, in compliance with the GFR 2017 Rule 133(3).


Furthermore, bidders are informed that the evaluation of the bids will be conducted through the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method. Under this method, technical proposals will carry a weightage of 70%, while financial proposals will account for 30% of the total evaluation score. This ensures a balanced approach that not only considers the cost but also the quality of the proposals submitted.


The budget allocated for this project is in Indian Rupees (INR), and the eligibility period for participation is set at 900 days from the date of announcement. It is imperative for the Bidder to navigate the bid process within this timeframe, ensuring compliance with all requirements to secure successful participation in the tender. Failure to adhere to the conditions may result in disqualification from the bidding process.

sections.title: Annexure II · General Undertaking
sections.hint: No conflict of interest, not debarred, no litigation, no misrepresentation.
sections.body:
This General Undertaking is a vital component of the application process for the tender. By submitting this undertaking, the bidder ensures adherence to fundamental ethical standards and compliance with the tender's eligibility criteria.


The bidder confirms that there exists no conflict of interest that could impede a fair and transparent evaluation of the tender submissions. Additionally, the bidder declares that they have not been debarred from participating in any public procurement activities, ensuring the integrity of the bidding process.


The bidder further attests that there are no ongoing litigations that could affect their capability to fulfill the obligations outlined in the tender. This affirmation is critical for maintaining a risk-free engagement and ensuring that the bidding entity is viable for the required 900-day period.


Moreover, the bidder acknowledges that all representations made in the submission are truthful and comprehensive, thereby avoiding any form of misrepresentation. Any inaccuracies in the provided information may lead to disqualification from the tender process.


By signing this General Undertaking, the bidder commits to maintaining the highest standards of integrity and transparency in their dealings with the tendering authority, in line with the eligibility criteria defined for Central/State Govt Organizations, PSUs, and Autonomous Bodies per GFR 2017 Rule 133(3).

sections.title: Annexure III · Brief Description & Scope of Work
sections.hint: Detailed scope of work / deliverables / milestones / stakeholders.
sections.body:
This annexure provides a comprehensive description of the scope of work as well as the deliverables, milestones, and stakeholders involved in the tender. The project is set to be executed within a period of 900 days and is open to Central and State Government Organizations, Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), and Autonomous Bodies as per GFR 2017 Rule 133(3).

The deliverables for this project include:

  • Development of detailed project plans that outline the implementation strategy.
  • Regular progress reports submitted bi-monthly, detailing milestones achieved.
  • Final project report that encapsulates the outcomes, challenges faced, and recommendations.

Key milestones have been identified and are to be strictly adhered to, including:

  1. Completion of initial project assessment within the first 90 days.
  2. Mid-project review at the 450-day mark, assessing alignment with initial goals.
  3. Final evaluation and project closure within the stipulated 900 days.

Stakeholders in this project comprise representatives from the contracting organization, project implementation team members, and external auditors, all of whom will play a crucial role in ensuring successful project delivery.

The evaluation of bids will apply a Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method, with a weightage of 70% for technical aspects and 30% for financial considerations.

sections.title: Annexure IV · Memorandum of Understanding
sections.hint: Framework MoU — roles, payment terms, dispute resolution, termination.
sections.body:
Annexure IV · Memorandum of Understanding

This Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) serves as the framework for collaboration between the involved parties throughout the project's duration, which spans 900 days. The MoU delineates the roles and responsibilities of each party involved, ensuring clarity in operations and accountability.

Roles: Each party shall designate a lead representative responsible for the coordination and execution of activities. The roles will be clearly defined in the detailed project documentation, which adheres to the guidelines set forth by the GFR 2017 Rule 133(3) pertaining to Central/State Government Organizations, PSU, or Autonomous Bodies.

Payment Terms: Payments shall be executed in accordance with the milestones set in the project timeline, subject to satisfactory performance as assessed through the QCBS evaluation method, with a technical score weighted at 70 and financial at 30. The payment structure will be designed to incentivize timely and quality delivery.

Dispute Resolution: In the event of conflicts arising during the execution of this MoU, parties agree to engage in good faith negotiations to resolve disputes amicably. Should negotiations fail, an independent arbitration process will be initiated as a means to facilitate resolution.

Termination: This MoU may be terminated by any party with a written notice of 30 days if substantial breaches occur, thereby ensuring the integrity and intention behind the collaboration remains intact.

sections.title: Annexure V · Integrity Pact
sections.hint: Anti-bribery, anti-corruption, gift and hospitality clauses per CVC guidelines.
sections.body:
The Integrity Pact is a crucial instrument aimed at ensuring transparency and fostering trust in the procurement process. This annexure delineates the anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and gift and hospitality clauses that align with the guidelines set forth by the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).


To promote ethical conduct, all bidders are required to adhere to the following principles:

  • Neither the bidder nor any of its representatives shall offer, promise, or give any bribe or consider it acceptable, whether directly or indirectly, to any public servant.
  • All parties involved in the tender process must refrain from any form of corruption, coercion, or introduction of unfair competitive practices.
  • Gifts or hospitality that may influence the decision-making process shall not be extended to or accepted from any stakeholders related to the procurement.

The successful bidder will sign an Integrity Pact with the procuring entity, ensuring compliance with these stipulations throughout the contract duration that spans 900 days.


In instances of breach of the Integrity Pact, appropriate actions will be taken, including termination of the contract and consideration for legal recourse. All Central / State Government Organizations, Public Sector Undertakings, and Autonomous Bodies as per GFR 2017 Rule 133(3) are eligible to participate, with evaluation conducted through the QCBS method, assigning 70% weight to technical parameters and 30% to financial proposals.

sections.title: Annexure VI · Sample Milestone Chart
sections.hint: Chronological deliverables + payment tranches + acceptance criteria.
sections.body:
Annexure VI · Sample Milestone Chart

This annexure outlines the chronological deliverables, payment tranches, and acceptance criteria for the project over a period of 900 days.

  • Milestone 1: Project Initiation
    • Deliverable: Completion of project kickoff meeting and submission of project plan.
    • Payment Tranche: 10% of the total contract value upon acceptance of the project plan.
    • Acceptance Criteria: Approval of the project plan by the designated authority.
  • Milestone 2: Mid-term Review
    • Deliverable: Submission of progress report and preliminary findings.
    • Payment Tranche: 20% of the total contract value upon review of the report.
    • Acceptance Criteria: Acceptance of the progress report by the review committee.
  • Milestone 3: Final Submission
    • Deliverable: Delivery of the final project report and documentation.
    • Payment Tranche: 50% of the total contract value upon delivery.
    • Acceptance Criteria: Approval of the final report and satisfaction of the stated objectives.
  • Milestone 4: Project Closure
    • Deliverable: Conducting of project closure meeting.
    • Payment Tranche: 20% of the total contract value after successful project closure.
    • Acceptance Criteria: Completion and acceptance of all deliverables by the project stakeholders.

sections.title: Annexure VII · Bid Security Declaration Form
sections.hint: In lieu of EMD — declaration that the bidder will be debarred if bid withdrawn during validity.
sections.body:
The Bid Security Declaration Form, as referenced in this Annexure VII, serves as a mandatory declaration in lieu of the Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) for bidders participating in this tender. All bidders must provide this form to assure the Authority of their commitment throughout the bid validity period of 900 days.

By submitting the Bid Security Declaration, the bidder confirms that if they withdraw their bid during the stated validity period, they will be subject to debarment from future bidding activities with the Authority. This declaration holds significant importance, reinforcing the integrity of the bidding process and safeguarding the interests of all parties involved. It is crucial that bidders understand the implications of this declaration and the commitment they are making by participating in this tender.

Bidders must ensure that their declaration is duly signed and submitted as part of their bid documents. Failure to provide this form or any indication of withdrawal from the bid within the stipulated time frame will lead to exclusion from the tender process.

Moreover, it is vital for bidders to meet the eligibility criteria specified, which includes participation from Central/State Government Organizations, Public Sector Undertakings, or Autonomous Bodies as per the GFR 2017 Rule 133(3).

For evaluation, the method employed will be the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS), allocating weights of 70% to Technical evaluation and 30% to Financial evaluation.

sections.title: Annexure VIII · Bank Solvency Certificate
sections.hint: Format of solvency certificate from a scheduled bank — issued within X months.
sections.body:
The Bank Solvency Certificate is a crucial document required as part of this tender submission. It must be acquired from a scheduled bank and should validate the financial stability and creditworthiness of the bidder. This certificate is to be issued within the last six months to ensure that the information is current and relevant.


The certificate must specifically outline the following details:

  • Name and address of the bank issuing the certificate.
  • Name of the financial entity (bidder), including registration details if applicable.
  • Confirmation that the bidder maintains an operative account with the bank.
  • Details of the current account balance and any fixed deposits held by the bidder with this bank.
  • A statement asserting the financial standing of the bidder, indicating their ability to fulfill the contract obligations.
  • The validity period of the certificate, which should extend beyond the tender evaluation period.
  • The emission date, which must fall within the stipulated timeframe of the last six months.

The Solvency Certificate is particularly critical for bidders from Central and State Government Organizations, Public Sector Undertakings, and Autonomous Bodies as specified by GFR 2017 Rule 133(3). In this evaluation process, the financial credentials being robust will significantly contribute to the overall score, as the evaluation methodology is based on a QCBS approach, allocating a weightage of 70% to technical criteria and 30% to financial criteria.

sections.title: Form A · General Information · Organization Details
sections.hint: Legal name, address, CIN/GSTIN/PAN, incorporation date, key contacts.
sections.body:
The following details are required for the completion of the General Information Form A. Please ensure that all information is accurate and up-to-date. This section is critical for establishing eligibility and assessing the organizational capability as per the tender requirements.

  • Legal Name: Please provide the full legal name of your organization as registered.
  • Address: Include the complete physical address of your organization, including city and postal code.
  • CIN/GSTIN/PAN: Submit the Corporate Identification Number (CIN), Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN), and Permanent Account Number (PAN) as applicable.
  • Incorporation Date: State the date on which your organization was incorporated.
  • Key Contacts: Please list the names, positions, email addresses, and phone numbers of key contact persons who can provide further information regarding this tender. Ensure that these contacts are accessible during the entire tendering period of 900 days.

Eligible bidders must meet the criteria as outlined under Central/State Government Organizations/PSU/Autonomous Body according to GFR 2017 Rule 133(3). Proposals will undergo an evaluation process based on the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, assigning a weightage of 70% to technical evaluation and 30% to financial evaluation.

sections.title: Form B · Strength of Key Technical Personnel
sections.hint: Table of designations, headcount, qualifications, experience floor.
sections.body:
In this section, bidders are required to provide detailed information regarding the key technical personnel who will be involved in the execution of the project. The submission must include a table listing the designations, headcount, qualifications, and relevant experience of each team member. The qualifications must meet the specified minimum standards to ensure competency for the project’s requirements.


The following format should be used to present the information:


  • Designation: Specify the role/title of the personnel.
  • Headcount: Indicate the number of individuals assigned to each designated role.
  • Qualifications: Provide details of the academic and professional qualifications of each team member.
  • Experience: Outline the relevant experience, including years of service and projects completed, ensuring it meets the required floor of experience relative to the complexity of the current project.

All information provided should align with the eligibility criteria set forth under the Central/State Government Organizations, PSU, or Autonomous Bodies as per GFR 2017 Rule 133(3). The evaluation of the technical proposal will follow the QCBS methodology, weighing technical qualifications at 70% and financial proposals at 30% over the 900-day project period.

sections.title: Form C · List of Similar Projects Completed (Last 7 Years)
sections.hint: Client, work name, value, start–end date, current value indexation, contact for verification.
sections.body:
The tenderers are required to submit Form C, which should include a comprehensive list of similar projects completed within the last seven years. The following details must be provided for each project:

  • Client: Name of the organization for which the project was completed.
  • Work Name: Title or description of the completed project.
  • Project Value: Original value of the project in INR at the time of completion.
  • Project Duration: Start and end dates of the project, formatted as DD/MM/YYYY.
  • Current Value Indexation: Any adjustments to the original project value to reflect current price indices, if applicable.
  • Contact for Verification: A representative from the client organization who can verify the completed work. This must include the contact name, phone number, and email address.

It is important that the completed projects are relevant in nature and scope to the tender being bid for. This will aid in evaluating the eligibility of the tenderers based on their experience. The evaluation will follow the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, with a weightage of 70% allocated to the technical proposal and 30% to the financial proposal.

Ensure all details are accurate and verifiable to support the credibility of the submitted information.

sections.title: Form D · Major Projects in Progress
sections.hint: Ongoing engagements including % completion, expected finish date, value.
sections.body:
Form D · Major Projects in Progress

In this section, bidders are required to provide detailed information regarding any major projects they are currently engaged in. This information is vital for evaluating the bidder's experience and capacity to handle the tendered project. Below are the specifics to be included:

  • Project Name: Clearly state the title of the project.
  • Client/Organization: Indicate the organization under which the project is being executed.
  • Percentage Completion: Provide an estimated percentage of the project that has been completed to date.
  • Expected Finish Date: Mention the anticipated date of project completion.
  • Project Value: Specify the total value of the project in Indian Rupees (INR).

It is crucial that all responses are accurate and substantiated, as they will be evaluated under the prescribed Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, which comprises 70% technical and 30% financial criteria. Bidders must also ensure eligibility as outlined under the GFR 2017 Rule 133(3) pertaining to engagements with Central or State Government Organizations, Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), or Autonomous Bodies.

This form aims to establish the credibility of the bidders while providing clear insights into their operational capabilities and commitments, in light of the 900-day project period stipulated in this tender.

sections.title: Form E · Turnover for Last Five Years
sections.hint: Y1–Y5 turnover + audited financial statements + CA UDIN.
sections.body:
The bidder is required to submit Form E, detailing the turnover for the last five financial years, labeled as Y1 to Y5. The information provided in this form is critical for assessing the financial viability of the bidder in relation to the project requirements.


In addition to Form E, bidders must include their audited financial statements for each of the last five years. These documents should reflect the true and fair view of the financial position of the bidder and lend credibility to the declared turnover figures. Each statement must be duly signed by a Chartered Accountant (CA), accompanied by the CA’s unique document identification number (UDIN) to ensure authenticity.


Referencing the eligibility criteria, participating bidders should be registered under the Central or State Government Organizations, Public Sector Undertakings (PSU), or Autonomous Bodies as per GFR 2017 Rule 133(3). This stipulation is essential for maintaining a competitive and fair bidding process.


Furthermore, the evaluation will follow the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method, with a weightage of 70% for technical evaluation and 30% for financial evaluation, ensuring a holistic review of both technical capabilities and financial stability.


All submissions must be completed within a period of 900 days, and ensuring timely and accurate documentation will be pivotal in aligning with the tender specifications.

sections.title: Form F · 'To Whom So Ever It May Concern' Certificate
sections.hint: Client-issued capability + performance certificate template.
sections.body:
This section provides the template for the 'To Whom So Ever It May Concern' Certificate, which is issued by the client to affirm the vendor's capability and performance under previous contracts. The format outlined below must be adhered to by all applicants; deviations may lead to disqualification.

Certificate Template

To Whom So Ever It May Concern,

This is to certify that [Vendor Name], having registered office at [Vendor Address], has successfully executed the following projects with our organization:

  • [Project 1 Name] - Description of services rendered and outcomes achieved.
  • [Project 2 Name] - Description of services rendered and outcomes achieved.

During the contract period which spanned from [Start Date] to [End Date], [Vendor Name] demonstrated exceptional competency in meeting performance standards and objectives that were stipulated in the agreements.

The services delivered were compliant with all relevant regulations and enjoyed satisfactory feedback from our stakeholders.

In conclusion, we wish to acknowledge the expertise and reliability shown by [Vendor Name] throughout our association. This certificate is issued upon the vendor’s request for their further business pursuance.

Issued on [Date] by [Client Name].

name: TEST_v46f QA Wales Highway 1791964175 · GB master

header.work_description: Design, build and commissioning of a two-lane highway including bridges, drainage, signage and safety barriers
header.eligibility: minimum turnover GBP 30 million for last 3 years, prior highway experience
dpr_warnings: Chunk pass returned no sections — used generic 5-section fallback

sections.title: Dpr 1
sections.body:
The project involves the construction of a 40km highway in Wales, ensuring enhanced connectivity and improved transportation efficiency in the region.


The estimated budget for this ambitious initiative is approximately GBP 12 million, with a projected duration of 18 months for completion. This timeframe underscores a commitment to timely delivery while adhering to the highest standards of quality.


The scope of the project includes:

  • Design, build, and commissioning of a two-lane highway
  • Construction of bridges
  • Implementation of effective drainage systems
  • Installation of signage
  • Incorporation of safety barriers

The client overseeing this project is the Welsh Government, which highlights the significance and governmental backing of this infrastructure endeavor.


For the evaluation of proposals, the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method will be employed, with technical aspects accounting for 70% of the evaluation and financial aspects making up 30%. This approach ensures that both quality and cost are given due consideration in the selection process.


Interested bidders should note that an Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) of 2% of the tender value will be required. Additionally, bids must maintain a validity period of 120 days to ensure the stability and reliability of the offers submitted.


The project will span the Cardiff to Swansea corridor, strategically positioned to maximize the impact on regional transport efficiency. Contractor eligibility requires a minimum turnover of GBP 30 million over the last three years and prior experience in highway construction.

sections.title: Dpr 2
sections.body:
The scope of work for the project involves the comprehensive design, build, and commissioning of a two-lane highway extending over 40 kilometers in Wales, specifically along the corridor connecting Cardiff to Swansea. The project is backed by a budget of GBP 12 million and is expected to span a duration of 18 months.

Key deliverables include:

  • Construction of a two-lane highway
  • Development of necessary infrastructure including:
    1. Bridges
    2. Drainage systems
    3. Signage
    4. Safety barriers

It is essential that all work complies with standards set forth by the Welsh Government, the client for this project. The evaluation of bids will be conducted using a Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method, where 70% of the score will come from technical evaluation and 30% will be based on financial aspects.

Prospective contractors must adhere to the following eligibility criteria:

  • A minimum turnover of GBP 30 million for the past three years
  • Prior experience in highway construction projects

Additionally, the Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) required is calculated as 2% of the tender value. The bids submitted must remain valid for a duration of 120 days to ensure adequate evaluation and selection processes.

sections.title: Dpr 3
sections.body:
The construction project entails a significant budget allocation of GBP 12 million for the development of a 40km highway in Wales. Spanning approximately 18 months, the project aims to fulfill the scope of design, build, and commissioning of a two-lane highway that will include essential components such as bridges, drainage, signage, and safety barriers, ensuring compliance with safety and regulatory standards.

The Welsh Government is the client overseeing this project, which demands a thorough understanding and experience in highway construction from bidders. The eligibility criteria for contractors are stringent, requiring a minimum turnover of GBP 30 million over the last three years, as well as prior experience in similar highway projects.

To ensure the financial viability and commitment to the project, an Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) of 2% of the tender value will be required at the time of submission. This financial assurance demonstrates the contractor's seriousness regarding the tender process and helps mitigate risks associated with project procurement.

The evaluation of tenders will utilize a Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, which allocates 70% of the weight to technical criteria and 30% to financial proposals. This approach prioritizes the quality of the project while still considering the cost-effectiveness of proposals submitted.

Additionally, the bid validity is stipulated at 120 days, ensuring that ample time is provided for a thorough evaluation of the submitted tenders and that contractual commitments can be clarified and solidified. The project is geographically situated along the Cardiff to Swansea corridor, making it a crucial route for enhancing infrastructure and connectivity in the region.

sections.title: Dpr 4
sections.body:
The timeline for the project is essential for ensuring that all phases are executed efficiently and effectively to meet strategic objectives. The key milestones are outlined within the project schedule, which must be adhered to by the selected contractor. Adherence to the timeline is critical for the successful completion of deliverables and avoiding any potential penalties.

Milestones to be achieved during the project include:

  • Milestone 1: Completion of initial project planning and design submissions within the first month.
  • Milestone 2: Approval of technical specifications and drawings by stakeholders by the end of the second month.
  • Milestone 3: Procurement of necessary materials and resources completed by the third month.
  • Milestone 4: Foundation and structural work to commence by the fourth month.
  • Milestone 5: Mid-project review and adjustments to be presented by the end of the sixth month.
  • Milestone 6: Completion of all construction activities by the end of the ninth month.
  • Milestone 7: Final inspections and project handover to commence by the tenth month and conclude by the eleventh month.

Overall, the project timeline is structured to allow for a thorough, phased approach to construction and completion, ensuring that critical benchmarks are met while maintaining high standards of quality. Regular updates and communication will be required throughout the process to address any risks or delays promptly. The project is expected to wrap up successfully in the allotted time frame, contingent upon diligent adherence to the above milestones.

sections.title: Dpr 5
sections.body:
The eligibility criteria for bidders in this tender are designed to ensure that only qualified contractors are considered for the project. Bidders must demonstrate a minimum turnover of **GBP 30 million** over the last three fiscal years. Additionally, it is essential that contractors have prior experience in highway construction, affirming their capability to undertake the project’s scope successfully.

The evaluation method adopted for this tender follows the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) system. Under this methodology, technical proposals will account for **70%** of the total evaluation score, while financial proposals will contribute to **30%**. This ensures that both the quality of work and cost-efficiency are adequately prioritized during the selection process.

Interested bidders should also be aware of the following key stipulations:

  • Earnest Money Deposit (EMD): Bidders are required to submit an EMD amounting to **2%** of the tender value.
  • Bid Validity: Proposals must remain valid for **120 days** from the submission date.
  • Project Location: The highway construction will take place along the corridor from Cardiff to Swansea.
  • Estimated Budget: The total budget allocated for the project is **GBP 12 million**.
  • Project Duration: The anticipated duration for the completion of the highway construction is **18 months**.

All prospective bidders are encouraged to thoroughly review the criteria and evaluation methods to ensure eligibility and to enhance their proposal's competitiveness. Successful completion of this project will significantly contribute to improving infrastructure within the region, and we look forward to receiving high-quality bids that reflect the necessary expertise and financial stability.
